subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender normalizes to destination_caller_id, should the branch only rewrite from a canonical peer candidate and drop or ignore the payload when no canonical peer can be trusted?
rationale: The sender repair occurs before iMessage allowlist, pairing, route, and reply decisions, so the permanent identity-boundary behavior needs maintainer ownership rather than a speculative fallback.

options.title: Canonical Repair, Fail Closed When Untrusted
options.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, rewrite only from a canonical peer candidate, and drop or ignore unrecoverable sender==destination payloads before access control.

options.title: Canonical Repair Only
options.body: Fix the weak comparison and live-prove the branch, but leave unrecoverable payloads on the existing downstream behavior for a later issue.

options.title: Pause For Narrower Root Cause
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is not this race, pause this branch and ask for a narrower iMessage report or replacement PR.

recommendation.title: Canonical Repair, Fail Closed When Untrusted
recommendation.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, rewrite only from a canonical peer candidate, and drop or ignore unrecoverable sender==destination payloads before access control.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged destination_caller_id and self-chat fixes are the closest current history for this identity boundary.
